# Section A2 — SEO Alignment 🔎

Phase A (repo-only). Read [PRE-LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md](../../PRE-LAUNCH-CHECKLIST.md) execution rules first. Enumerate all item IDs before starting; write your ledger to `reports/pre-launch/A2.md`.

**Ground truth:** [src/data/seo-map.mjs](../../src/data/seo-map.mjs) — the per-page keyword plan authored during onboarding. **Working artifact:** `reports/pre-launch/seo-matrix.md`, generated by `npm run preflight` — one row per page with the built title/H1/description and exact-match keyword columns. Judge alignment **row by row on the matrix**, never from memory of the pages.

The matrix's keyword columns are exact-substring heuristics. A ❌ cell is not automatically a failure — "roof repair" vs "roofing repairs" may be an acceptable variant. That call is exactly what this section exists for.

| ID | Action | Check | How to Verify | If Failed |
|----|--------|-------|---------------|-----------|
| A2-1 | 👁️ VERIFY ONLY | **SEO map is complete** | Open `src/data/seo-map.mjs`. Every indexable, non-navigational page has `primaryKeyword`, `intent`, `title`, `description`, and `h1` filled in — no empty strings, no TODO comments. This is an onboarding deliverable (ONBOARDING.md §4): the agent must not invent keywords at launch time. | ⏸ BLOCKED — report exactly which routes/fields are missing and request the keyword map from the human. Do NOT fill in keywords yourself; a launch check against self-invented targets is circular. |
| A2-2 | 🔧⚠️ FIX WITH REVIEW | **Per-row alignment judgment** | For every indexable row in `seo-matrix.md`, judge each ❌ keyword cell: is a close variant of the keyword genuinely present, or is the element misaligned? Criteria per row: (a) keyword or close variant front-loaded in the title, ≤ 60 chars total; (b) slug matches the keyword's core terms; (c) H1 aligned with the title but not identical; (d) description 150–160 chars containing keyword + value proposition + CTA; (e) keyword or variant within the opening copy (~first 100 words). Record a verdict per row: ALIGNED / VARIANT-OK (name the variant) / MISALIGNED (name the element). | For MISALIGNED elements: rewrite the title/description/H1/opening copy in the page source (and update the map if the map itself was wrong — map and page must agree afterward). Re-run `npm run preflight` and confirm the matrix reflects the fix. All wording changes flagged for human review. |
| A2-3 | 🔧⚠️ FIX WITH REVIEW | **No keyword cannibalization** | Compare `primaryKeyword` values across all indexable rows (preflight PF-20 flags exact duplicates; you must also judge near-duplicates — "roof repair springfield" vs "roof repair springfield mo" target the same query). No two indexable pages may compete for the same query. | Propose which page keeps the keyword and what the other page should target instead. This changes the client's content strategy → always flag for human decision; only apply after sign-off unless the resolution is obvious (e.g., a boilerplate page accidentally reusing the homepage keyword). |
| A2-4 | 🔧 FIX | **Map, pages, and matrix converge** | After all fixes: `npm run preflight` shows no PF-20 errors, and every WARN remaining is a documented VARIANT-OK from A2-2. Paste the final PF-20 output and your per-row verdict table as evidence. | Iterate A2-2/A2-3 until convergence. If a row cannot converge (e.g., client-mandated title conflicts with the keyword), record ⚠️ WARNING with the conflict stated for human resolution. |

> **🛑 CHECKPOINT:** Write the ledger (include the full per-row verdict table), then run the verification pass per the runbook before starting A3.
